lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Decision Analysis and Expected Value Capstone
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: evaluating and comparing decision strategies

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: Costs $5, pays $40 with probability 1/10. Expected value?
Premium $30, payout $1000 with probability 1/50. Expected profit?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $24 and Option B has expected payoff $8. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option A; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.

items.prompt: A game costs $2 to play. It pays $20 with probability 1/4 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $3; the game is favourable to the player
$5; the game is favourable to the player
$18; the game is favourable to the player
$-2; the game is unfavourable to the player

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $10 and pays out $315 with probability 1/45. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $6 and Option B has expected payoff $13. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.
Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning two faces to each.
choices: Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.

items.prompt: A game costs $6 to play. It pays $204 with probability 1/17 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $6; the game is favourable to the player
$198; the game is favourable to the player
$-6; the game is unfavourable to the player
$12; the game is favourable to the player
